# Copilot instructions: apartment planner

A small 3D interior planning tool for one specific apartment (Wohnung 33, 3.5 Zimmer). The apartment, the
furniture catalogue, the material presets and the layouts are data files. The code is a generic engine that reads
them at runtime. It runs locally (`npm start`) and as a website built from `main`:
https://lettersfromfelix.github.io/interior-design-tool/.

## The rule that matters most

- **To add furniture, only create files in `catalogue/`, never modify engine code** (`src/`, `server/`). Follow
  [CATALOGUE.md](../CATALOGUE.md): format, placement types, material slots, examples and a checklist.
- For a new colour or finish, add a preset to `data/materials.json` (format in [docs/DATA.md](../docs/DATA.md)).
- If the data formats can't express what the user wants, say so and ask. Change code only when the user asks for
  that change.

## Where things are

| Path | What | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `catalogue/` | furniture, one item per file (or per folder with its 3D model) | auto-discovered; file name = `id` |
| `data/apartment.json` | the fixed apartment: rooms, walls, doors, windows, kitchen, built-ins, with provenance | change only for tape measurements or corrections from the user, see below |
| `data/materials.json` | material presets (`wood.*`, `fabric.*`, `paint.*`, `floor.*`, …) | extend freely |
| `layouts/` | the user's layouts, one JSON file each | see [Layouts](#layouts) |
| `schemas/` | JSON Schemas | generated by `npm run schemas`, never edit |
| `src/core/schema/` | the Zod schemas: the single source of every data format | |
| `docs/DATA.md` | data formats, coordinate system, measurement workflow, the file API and the website build | |
| `.github/workflows/pages.yml` | checks, builds and publishes the website on every push to `main` | |
| `data/underlay/` | the floor-plan underlay image, made from the PDF by `tools/floorplan/underlay.py` | local only, git-ignored, never in the website build; never commit it |
| `reference/` | the original floor plan PDF and photos | local only, git-ignored (they show the address); never commit them, nor any crop of or texture made from a photo (recreate finishes as patterns and colours in `data/materials.json`) |

## The website and the public repository

- The repository is **public**, and everything in `data/`, `catalogue/` and `layouts/` is published on the website.
  Never commit the street address, photos, the floor-plan PDF or anything made from them (`reference/`,
  `data/underlay/`), and only add 3D models whose licence allows publishing them.
- A push to `main` rebuilds the website (the **Website** workflow: validate, tests, type check, lint, build,
  deploy). New furniture, data and published layouts appear there after that; push only when the user asks.
- On the website, visitors' layouts live in their browser, not in the repository. They share them as downloaded
  files; a layout file someone sends goes into `layouts/` (or the user opens it with **Open file…**).

## Units and coordinates

- **Centimetres** everywhere; angles in **degrees**.
- **Plan coordinates** `[x, z]`: +x is right on the floor-plan sheet, +z is down the sheet. **+y is up**; the floor is
  at y = 0 and the ceiling at `ceilingHeight` (255 cm). Three.js uses the same axes.
- **Rotations** of placed items turn clockwise seen from above. At 0° the item's front (+z) faces down the plan.
- **Item frame:** origin at the bottom centre of the `dimensions` box, x = width, y = up, z = depth, front = +z.
  Standing in front of the item, looking at it, +x is on your right (so clearance `left` / `right` are as seen from
  the front).
- **Part rotations** are applied z, then x, then y, around the item's axes: y clockwise seen from above, x and z tilt
  by the right-hand rule.
- **Walls:** `left` / `right` are as seen walking from a wall's `start` to its `end`; one side of a wall is
  `"<wallId>:left|right"`.
- **North:** `north.planUpBearing` in `data/apartment.json` is the compass bearing of plan-up (about 49°).

## Validation

Run after every data change, and fix what they report:

| Command | When |
|---|---|
| `npm run validate` | after any change to `catalogue/`, `data/` or `layouts/`: the app's own rules; needs 0 errors, aim for 0 warnings |
| `npm test` | after code changes, and when you change `CATALOGUE.md` or an item it shows (the examples must match the files) |
| `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` | after code changes (ESLint also enforces the layers below) |
| `npm run schemas` | after changing a Zod schema in `src/core/schema/` |
| `npm run checklist` | after changing provenance or checks in `data/apartment.json` |

The schemas are strict: unknown properties are errors, ids are kebab-case, and preset ids look like
`"<group>.<name>"`. A broken file never breaks the app; it is listed in the **Issues** panel and left out.

## Layouts

- Human-readable JSON in `layouts/`, format in [docs/DATA.md](../docs/DATA.md#layoutsjson). The app autosaves and
  reloads a file that changes on disk, so you can read and edit layouts while it runs.
- They are the user's files, and they are tracked in git (the user's decision) and published with the website.
  Don't create, change or delete them unless asked, and commit changes to them only when the user asks, not as part
  of other work. `layouts/demo.json` is an example layout. `layouts/.trash/` (deleted layouts) is git-ignored.
- To place furniture for the user, edit the layout file: `position` is the item's bottom centre `[x, z]`, `rotation`
  is in degrees, and items standing on another item have `parent` and positions relative to it.

## The apartment data

- Every value has `provenance` (`confidence`, `source`, `note`). Uncertain values have low or medium confidence and
  appear in the tape-measure checklist, `docs/measurement-checklist.md`.
- To apply tape measurements, follow "Applying tape measurements" in [docs/DATA.md](../docs/DATA.md). Measured values
  get `source: "measured"`, `confidence: "high"`.
- `tools/floorplan/build_apartment.py` generated the file from the PDF and holds the user's earlier decisions as
  constants (door styles, how far doors open). It refuses to overwrite measured data; after measuring, edit
  `data/apartment.json` directly.

## Code conventions (only when the user asks for code changes)

- Layers, enforced by ESLint: nothing in `src/` imports data files (they are fetched at runtime); `src/core` is pure
  TypeScript (no Three.js, React or store); `src/engine` doesn't import React or `src/ui`.
- The engine contains no room, wall or item ids: everything it draws comes from the data.
- Every layout change is a pure command in `src/core/layout/commands.ts`, which is what undo/redo relies on.
- Data access goes through the file backend (`src/data/fileBackend.ts`): `api.ts` (the dev server's file API) or
  `siteBackend.ts` (the website: build listings + `localStorage`). Code that works with files must work with both.
- `server/localFsApi.ts` is the only code that touches the disk at runtime; it writes only `layouts/*.json`.
  `server/staticSite.ts` reads the same folders at build time.
- URLs of the app's own files start with `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` (`/` locally, `/interior-design-tool/` on the
  website); use `assetUrl()` for files in the data folders.
- Keep the docs in step: `CATALOGUE.md`, `docs/DATA.md`, `README.md` and this file.

## Running

`npm start` serves the app at http://127.0.0.1:5180 and opens it (Node 22.12 or newer). It needs no network and no
services; everything runs on this laptop. `npm run build` and `npm run preview` build the website and serve it at
http://127.0.0.1:5181/interior-design-tool/ for a check before a push.
